title: Existing-Home Sales (NAR, October 2026 data) — the unconfounded edition before the FOMC-day print
source: EST: nar.realtor/newsroom/nar-statistical-news-release-schedule and its .docx twin /sites/default/files/2025-11/2026-nar-statistical-news-release-schedule.docx, both fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200), whose 2026 table reads "NOVEMBER | Thu., Nov. 12 | October Existing-Home Sales" under the standing note "All releases are distributed at 10 a.m. Eastern Time". Filed `estimate` rather than `confirmed` per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep; the source is the publisher's own forward calendar and its own initial research should promote it on the same page. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the existing-home-sales-2026-12-09 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06). Why it earns its own row rather than a line in that ledger: it is the CONTROL for the confound that makes the 12-09 print unreadable. On 2026-12-09 the EHS release shares its session with an FOMC SEP decision, whose 14:00 statement takes 85.8% of SPY's session range and compresses the print's own 10:00-11:00 hour to 26.0% against a 40.4% baseline (721 hourly sessions 2023-10-09 -> 2026-09-04, p=0.0006); the same compression holds for homebuilders (ITB 23.3% vs 35.8%, p=0.0027). 11-12 is an ordinary Thursday with no FOMC meeting on the Fed's 2026 panel, so it is the one nearby session where an EHS print's own tape can be read at all — and it prints the October level the 12-09 edition is measured against. It also sits four days before the 11-18 October Pending Home Sales Index and six days after the 11-09 wholesale print, so the corridor's housing and inventories lines can be separated on clean days before they collide. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the same measurement that keeps the December edition low: across 122 EHS release days since 2016 ITB (1.911% vs 1.839%, p=0.40) and XHB (1.693% vs 1.629%, p=0.46) are inert. Note for whoever picks this up: the Atlanta Fed's PostedUpdates does NOT name an existing-home-sales release on 2026-11-12 — GDPNow posts a vintage only on the release days it schedules, and 11-12 is not one — so this edition will have no same-day nowcast vintage to read, which is exactly what makes its TAPE the thing to measure. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
